anf_compare.notes: No ANF or other public-domain English of this homily; translated from the Greek.

bible_refs.note: Stephen cast out of the city and stoned: τῆς πόλεως ἔξω λαβόντες ~ ἐκβαλόντες ἔξω τῆς πόλεως ἐλιθοβόλουν.
Exact quotation: Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου.
κατ' εἰκόνα σήν echoes LXX κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν; the soul as what man holds after God's image.

choices.why: σχεδιάζω is to improvise; the stones stand in for the swords they lacked.
Hesychius frames the stoning as Stephen's sacrifice; the next sentence calls him the victim (θῦμα).

choices.term: παρὰ τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν τοῦ ποιμένος
choices.why: The second lamb is Christ; 'the Shepherd's Lamb' keeps the genitive without choosing between readings.
rejected: beside the Lamb who is the Shepherd

choices.why: κλαυθμών is a place of weeping; it stands in apposition to Hades.

pass_a_gloss: [continuing: and slings of stones … the holy laws] followed upon the doctrines. Being at a loss for weapons, they armed themselves from the earth; swords not being present, they improvised stones in their right hands, and having taken [him] outside the city they were sacrificing. For the old Jerusalem was not fitting for the victim; but the lamb had to be slaughtered beside the lamb, the [lamb] of the Shepherd; there the soldier had to receive the pledges of the victory, where the King fixed the trophy against all. §26 But what kind of provision for the journey of his end was he taking? Prayer and the incense from it; and putting off the flesh he put on the prayer. And what was the prayer? 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit', that is: You take what is yours; the deposit which you gave, take back; the pearl which you entrusted, receive; what I have according to your image, this I send to you. 'Receive my spirit'; for no longer into the place of weeping of Hades the … [sentence continues in u02-rem-early]
pass_b_english: With no weapons to hand, they armed themselves from the ground; for want of swords, they made do with stones in their right hands, and they took him outside the city and offered him in sacrifice (Acts 7:58). For the old Jerusalem was not a fitting place for this victim. The lamb had to be slain beside the Shepherd’s Lamb, and the soldier had to receive the pledges of victory there, where the King had set up the trophy over all.

But what provision did he take for the journey of his death? Prayer, and the incense that rises from it; and as he put off the flesh, he put on prayer. And what was the prayer? “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit” (Acts 7:59). That is: “Take what is yours; take back the deposit you gave; welcome the pearl you entrusted; what I bear after your image (Genesis 1:26), this I send to you. ‘Receive my spirit’; for no longer into Hades, the place of weeping, do the…”
source_text:
ἐπηκολούθουν δόγμασιν. Ὅπλων ἀποροῦντες, ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ὡπλίζοντο· ξίφων οὐ
παρόν των, λίθους ταῖς δεξιαῖς ἐσχεδίαζον, καὶ τῆς πόλεως ἔξω λα βόντες ἔθυον. Οὐ
γὰρ ἦν Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἡ παλαιὰ τῷ θύματι πρέ πουσα· ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν ἀμνὸν ἐχρῆν παρὰ
τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν τοῦ ποιμένος σφάζεσθαι, ἐκεῖ λαμβάνειν τὸν στρατιώτην τὰ τῆς νίκης
ἐνέχυρα, ἔνθα τὸ κατὰ πάντων τρόπαιον ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐπήξατο.
26 Ἀλλὰ ποῖον ἐλάμβανεν τῆς τελευτῆς ἐφόδιον; Προσευχὴν καὶ τὸ ἐκ ταύτης
θυμίαμα· καὶ τὴν σάρκα ἐκδυόμενος τὴν προσευχὴν ἐνεδύετο. Τί δὲ ἦν ἡ προσευχή;
«Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου», τουτέστιν· Σὺ λάβε τὸ σόν· ἣν ἔδωκας
παραθήκην ἀνάλαβε· ὃν ἐπίστευσας μαργαρίτην ὑπόδεξαι· ὃ κατ' εἰκόνα σὴν ἔχω,
τοῦτο πέμπω πρὸς σέ. «∆έξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου»· οὐκέτι γὰρ εἰς ᾅδου κλαυθμῶνος αἱ
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: The sentence that runs across the break (σφενδόναι λίθων τοῖς τῶν ἱερῶν νόμων | ἐπηκολούθουν δόγμασιν, 'and stones from slings followed the teachings of the holy laws') is translated whole at the end of the previous section, so the English here begins at the next sentence, Ὅπλων ἀποροῦντες.
ἐσχεδίαζον ('improvised') rendered 'made do with'; ἔθυον ('were sacrificing') kept as sacrifice, since Hesychius frames the stoning as Stephen's offering.

παρὰ τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν τοῦ ποιμένος: the second lamb is Christ; the genitive may mean 'the Shepherd's Lamb' or 'the Lamb who is the Shepherd'. The contrast with 'the old Jerusalem' assumes Christ suffered outside the gate (possible allusion to Hebrews 13:12, not cited inline). The trophy (τρόπαιον) is the cross.

Possible, uncertain allusions left out of the reading text: prayer as incense (Psalm 141:2, LXX 140:2; Revelation 8:3-4); the deposit (παραθήκη, 1 Timothy 6:20; 2 Timothy 1:12); the pearl (Matthew 13:46); κλαυθμών as 'place of weeping' (Psalm 84:6, LXX 83:7).
The section ends mid-sentence at αἱ; the clause continues 'souls of the righteous enter' in the next section.
